overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 15
overview.text: Students continue their exploration of residuals. Lesson 14 introduced residuals as the rationale for choosing the best-fit line. In this lesson, students calculate prediction errors for a data set and generalize residuals to predict the error of a value not included in the original data set.
outcomes: Students use the least squares line to predict values for a given data set.
Students use residuals to evaluate the accuracy of predictions based on the least squares line.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 15 Exit Ticket: Interpreting Residuals from a Line
exitTicket.prompt:
Exit Ticket

Meerkats have a gestation time of 70 days.

Use the equation of the least squares line from today's class, y=6.643+0.03974x, to predict the longevity of the meerkat. Remember x equals the gestation time in days, and y equals the longevity in years.

Approximately how close might your prediction be to the actual longevity of the meerkat? What was it (from class) that told you roughly how close a prediction might be to the true value?

According to your answers to parts (a) and (b), what is a reasonable range of possible values for the longevity of the meerkat?

The longevity of the meerkat is actually 10 years. Use this value and the predicted value that you calculated in part (a) to find the residual for the meerkat.
exitTicket.solution:
Meerkats have a gestation time of 70 days.

Use the equation of the least squares line from today's class, y=6.643+0.03974x, to predict the longevity of the meerkat. Remember x equals the gestation time in days, and y equals the longevity in years.

y=6.642+0.03974(70)=9.4

The predicted longevity of a meerkat is 9.4 years.

Approximately how close might your prediction be to the actual longevity of the meerkat? What was it (from class) that told you roughly how close a prediction might be to the true value?

The prediction would be within about 6 years. We looked at the residuals for the original data set and saw that the largest residual was around 6 years.

According to your answers to parts (a) and (b), what is a reasonable range of possible values for the longevity of the meerkat?

Between 3 and 15 years would be sensible.

The longevity of the meerkat is actually 10 years. Use this value and the predicted value that you calculated in part (a) to find the residual for the meerkat.

Residual=10-9.4=0.6

The residual for the meerkat is 0.6 years.

problemSet.title: Official Worksheet: Problem Set & Practice
problemSet.description: Master Interpreting Residuals from a Line through authentic curriculum practice problems. Check your work using the expandable teacher solution key below.

problems.prompt:
The time spent in surgery and the cost of surgery was recorded for six patients. The results and scatter plot are shown below.

Calculate the equation of the least squares line relating cost to time. (Indicate slope to the nearest tenth and y-intercept to the nearest whole number.)
problems.solution: y=1514+52.7x, where x represents time and y represents cost

problems.prompt: Draw the least squares line on the graph above. (Hint: Substitute x=30 into your equation to find the predicted y-value. Plot the point (30, your answer) on the graph. Then substitute x=180 into the equation, and plot the point. Join the two points with a straightedge.)
problems.solution: Plot the points (30, 3095) and (180, 11000) on the graph.

problems.prompt: What does the least squares line predict for the cost of a surgery that lasts 118 min.? (Calculate the cost to the nearest cent.)
problems.solution:
y=1514+52.7(118)=7732.60

The predicted cost for the surgery is $7,732.60.

problems.prompt: How much do you have to add to your answer to Problem 3 to get the actual cost of surgery for a surgery lasting 118 min.? (This is the residual.)
Show your answer to Problem 4 as a vertical line between the point for that person in the scatter plot and the least squares line.
Remember that the residual is the actual y-value minus the predicted y-value. Calculate the residual for the surgery that took 149 min. and cost $8,855.

Calculate the other residuals, and write all the residuals in the table below.

Suppose that a surgery took 100 min.

What does the least squares line predict for the cost of this surgery?
problems.solution:
x=100; y=1514+52.7(100)=6784

The predicted cost for the surgery is $6, 784.

problems.prompt: Would you be surprised if the actual cost of this surgery were $9,000? Why, or why not?
problems.solution: 9000-6784=2216. This is much larger than any of the residuals in the table, so it would be surprising to find that the surgery was this expensive.

problems.prompt: Interpret the slope of the least squares line.
problems.solution: The slope is 52.7 dollars per minute. Interpret this slope in the following way: For each additional minute in surgery, the cost of the surgery increases by $52.70.
